ShortDescription.Value: A better vanilla building menu: sorting, categories, filters and more details.

Publish.LongDescription:
A better version of the vanilla building menu, with sorting, categories and more details. Click any toolbar menu (Roads, Electricity, Education, Zones and the rest) and you get a panel instead of the row of icons.
* Grid, list, cards or table. Category tabs and a search box. * Sort by cost, upkeep, workers, capacity, lot, level or parking. * Group by type, theme, source, density, footprint, cost or progression. * Filter by unlocked, DLC, theme, asset pack, placement, role or source. Density has its own tabs. * Set a range for cost, upkeep, workers, capacity, lot width or lot depth. * Hover an asset to see its numbers and what unlocks it. * Building upgrades get names, cost and footprint too.
The list holds what the menu holds. Trees are under Landscaping; props, decals and hidden assets are not, and there is no object picker. Use Find It for those.
Works with Find It and does not replace it. Find It is a window over every asset in the game; this mod changes the toolbar menus. When Find It's window is open it takes the menu slot; this panel returns when it closes.
No Harmony patches, nothing saved to your city. Remove it any time.
**Options** (Options > Better Building Menu): switch back to the stock icon row; tile size; widen searches to every menu automatically.
Bugs and requests: the comments on this page.
Forked from Find It 1.5.8 by T. D. W. Thanks also to YenYang (UI), Algernon, Chameleon (icons) and Baka-gourd (focus handling).
This mod was developed with AI assistance (Anthropic's Claude), under human direction and review.
Publish.ChangeLog:
0.3.0
Changes * The build menu opens where the game's own does, at its size. Pick one of five Widths in Options › Better Building Menu, or drag the menu's right edge to one; every menu opens at it. * If you used an earlier version, the menu opens at the width nearest yours. * At the wider Widths the tool options move to the screen's left edge to make room. * The search, Sort, Filter, Group, View and close sit along the menu's top edge. Each control opens a list that a click elsewhere closes. View also offers Width and More options…. * The search box names the building Enter will place, or says All matches locked. * Control pane is now an option: off for new players, as you had it if you used an earlier version. * The pane's Reset menu is gone: Reset the build menu… in Options puts the options, the menu's size and each menu's View and Group back, after asking. * Pick the chosen sort again to reverse it. In Group, Category is now By tab and None is now No groups. * With a terraforming brush in hand, the menu stays open and answers your search and filters, as the game's does. * Enter in the search arms the best match, wherever it sits, however the list is sorted. * A sort's first click puts the best first, the most of a capacity or the lowest Cost or Upkeep; ties go to the cheaper building. * Sort by Households, Water capacity or Sewage capacity. * While Replace the vanilla build menu is off, the other options grey out and say why. * With a controller the game's own build menu shows; move the mouse and this one comes back, on the same menu. * The tabs sit along the menu's bottom edge, next to the toolbar: All with the menu's icon, then each tab's icon over its count, which follows your filters and search; a tab they empty keeps its place. * At the tabs' right end: the tab you are on; a value most of its buildings share, said once where the list has room, with its symbol (100 km/h unless shown), so only the others show theirs; and how many the list holds of how many match. The list's end shows only the button that loads more. * Education's school levels are named chips beside the Education tab. * A menu opens on the tab of the building you last picked from it, that building at the top; with nothing picked, on its first tab, and Education on its first school level. In Cards, or with few buildings, on All. Opening a menu clears the search. * Picking a sort, or clicking the lit tab, takes the list back to its top; so does going back to that building's tab. * While you type, Up and Down change the building Enter places, marked ↵ in the list, and Page Up and Page Down scroll it. Esc closes an open list, then clears the search, then closes the menu. * After Enter, a pick or closing the menu, the arrow keys move the camera again. The search box shows an outline while you type. * On a wider menu, each tab shows its name beside its icon where all fit. * A small mark under the menu points to its toolbar button. * The menu follows the game's Interface style and Interface transparency. * Each menu remembers its own View (List, Icons, Tiles or Cards) and Group, and its Sort until you quit. Options › Default view, Auto at first, sets the rest: a list for most menus, icons for big catalogues like Landscaping, tiles for zones. Grid is now Tiles, Table is now List. * If you used an earlier version, Default view starts at your View: Grid as Tiles, Table as List. * List puts each building on a plate, 20 a screen, more when wider: its picture; its name, cut once with … to keep what tells it apart; its cost, a road's per cell (¢44/c); and, by a symbol, its speed, capacity, workers or lot. Above 100% text, Options › At large text picks More buildings or Whole names. * Tiles shows pictures with their cost, tags look-alikes with what tells them apart, and names the one you point at. Options › Tile size is set to 64, once; a size you pick after that stays. * A tile's tag shows a long cost in thousands or millions, and under a sort by a number, that number. * Icons shows pictures alone, 45 a screen; a family (Boulder 01–08) shows each number and shares a shade. * Point at a building for its card; Options › Hover card moves it to the game's detail slot or the tabs' end. * Each View says MS n while the city waits on that milestone, else Locked, and keeps the unique and built marks. * Typing searches the whole menu, best match first, and Sort reads Match. Clearing it brings back your tab and sort. * Cards are earlier versions' cards, three rows to the menu's height, each as wide as its name. * In All, each View names each tab with its count. A tab mostly locked lists what you can build first, then Locked, which a click folds away. * A menu with few buildings shows them bigger in the list. * At a wider Width, search results fill the columns under the search box first.
Fixed * A list that stops at 2,000 buildings says so, and how to narrow it. * Under Metric filters, a min or max that is not a number is outlined in red.
